title: Ingress/Egress Differential + Burst Minimums: Pilot Design for Hosted API Pricing
creator: Amira Patel
description: Goal: validate a directional (ingress vs egress) per-token pricing model combined with a small burst/minimum floor for short-lived streaming sessions. We want to reduce unit-cost leakage from long-input-heavy eval jobs while preserving developer ergonomics for typical chat and content-generation workloads. This ticket covers experiment definition, measurement plan, rollout gating, and enterprise contract language to reflect differential IO billing.
hypothesis: If we bill hosted API calls with asymmetric per-token rates (higher for egress/output tokens, lower for ingress/input tokens) and apply a short burst minimum for streamed sessions (to avoid per-connection metering noise), then (1) high-input, low-output eval workloads will see clearer unit economics and (2) average hosted revenue per active developer will increase without significant churn among mid-volume customers.
experiment_design: 1) Create two parallel billing cohorts: control (current symmetric token pricing) and variant (directional rates + streaming burst minimum). 2) Variant pricing: ingress token = $0.0000025/token, egress token = $0.000012/token. 3) Streaming burst floor: for streaming sessions < 5s or < 16 tokens output, charge a 1-token egress minimum (waives only for free-tier sandbox). 4) Implement opt-in via account flag for enterprise contracts while enabling rollout to a 10% random sample of self-serve accounts. 5) Metering: client handshake includes stream-start marker so backend can attribute minimums reliably. 6) Observation window: 6 weeks with interim look at 2-week checkpoint.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: Perceived complexity of directional billing may increase support overhead and confusion in invoices.
- Tradeoff: Setting burst minimum too low will fail to curb pathological short calls; too high will penalize legitimate micro-interactions.
- Risk: Some enterprise customers have committed quotas priced under symmetric assumptions — legal changes required.
- Operational: Metering accuracy for streamed partial frames must be validated to avoid double-counting during reconnects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Telemetry shows directional variant increases revenue per active developer by >= 3% without +10% increase in billing disputes.
- No more than 2% of streaming sessions are misattributed due to reconnect edge-cases during testing.
- Legal has approved amendments for new invoice line items and sample contract language included in enterprise SQ (security questionnaire) addendum.
- Docs and SDKs updated with clear examples and FAQ.

open_questions: What grace-window should apply to reconnected streaming sessions that resume within 10s?
Should free-tier developer sandboxes be exempt from burst minimums entirely, or apply a scaled-down minimum?
Do we present directional rates as separate line items or present a blended effective rate in the invoice summary?
